final_message:
I filled in the yellow cells of the test plan and saved it as `Completed Week One Test Plan.xlsx`. I couldn't send it, so there is a draft email to the plant manager for you to send. I re-read the workbook against the rules sheet. Each press has 3 or more changeovers, no day goes over 450 minutes, and no one goes over 2,250 minutes for the week.

**Crew:** the most senior people who are not on discipline.
- **Press 1:** TM19 is the operator and TM20 is the water spider.
- **Press 2:** TM17 is the operator and TM16 is the water spider.
- **Skipped:** TM18, TM13, TM12, TM05 and TM01, because they are on discipline.

**Schedule:** there is only one of each tool pack, so each pack runs on one press. Days 3–5 are not needed.

| Press | Day 1 | Day 2 | Weekly minutes per crew member |
|---|---|---|---|
| Press 1 | T1/0 then T12, 384 min | T14 then T16, 300 min | 684 |
| Press 2 | T3/0 then T6, 387 min | T8, 183 min | 570 |

**Material needed:** 1,120 lb of polymer and 1,160 yards of wire, using the exact amounts with no extra.
- **Polymer:** ABS 280 lb and TPO 280 lb, then 140 lb each for PVC, TPE, TPU and TPV.
- **Wire:** 200 yards each for G16, G14 and G12; 160 yards each for G8 and G6; 120 yards each for G1/0 and G3/0.

Things to know before it goes out:
- **Polymer pounds:** the FG BOM note says 50 lb per pack for G1/0TPO, but the BOM table says 20 lb. I used 20 lb. If 50 is right, the polymer totals are 2.5 times higher.
- **Labor totals in minutes:** the team member table is headed "Total Hours" but its section title says minutes rounded up. I entered minutes and noted it in the sheet.
- **Added columns:** I added two reference columns (Planned Day and Run Sequence) because the template has nowhere to show which day a part runs.
- **Missing folders:** the `workspace/` and `attachments/` folders from the brief were not in the folder, so I used only `reference_files/`. I found no registry saying which records were operative.

The sheet also has notes at the bottom with the purchase-package counts.

DONE
